laws.rule: Dartmoor National Park: backpack (wild) camping is welcome without the landowner's prior approval only in the areas shown on the park's interactive camping map, so check it before the trip. The park's code asks for a lightweight tent, one or two nights as part of a longer walk, out of sight of roads and buildings, no more than six people in a group, no open fires or barbecues, and litter taken home. Overnight stays in vehicles, campervans or motorhomes at the roadside or in car parks are not permitted under National Park byelaws; the park points those visitors to designated sites. It asks for extra care in the ground-nesting bird season, 1 March to 31 July. The page names no penalty.

Lake District National Park: the authority says wild camping is technically not permitted without the landowner's permission. It cannot allow camping on private land and does not permit it on the little land it owns. Camping in car parks or on roadside verges is not allowed at any time. The authority says wild camping is normally tolerated if you camp above the highest fell wall, away from towns and lake shores, light no fires, stay one night, keep to one or two tents and leave no trace, and that a landowner can order campers to move on. The page names no penalty.

In England an enclosed vehicle is smoke-free, so smoking in it is banned, when more than one person is present and a person under 18 is present (Smoke-free (Private Vehicles) Regulations 2015, reg 2, inserting reg 11(1A) into the Smoke-free (Exemptions and Vehicles) Regulations 2007; in force 1 October 2015). A caravan or motor caravan is exempt when it is stationary and not on a road, or when it is stationary on a road and being used as living accommodation (reg 11(7)).
laws.heading: Smoke-free (Private Vehicles) Regulations 2015, regs 1 and 2

laws.rule: Since 1 June 2025 it is an offence in England to supply, offer to supply or hold for supply a single-use vape (a vape not designed to be reused, such as one that cannot be refilled or recharged). The offence is aimed at shops and other suppliers, not at a visitor using a vape. A person guilty of the offence is liable on summary conviction to a fine (reg 4(2)). The regulations apply in England only.
laws.heading: Environmental Protection (Single-use Vapes) (England) Regulations 2024 (SI 2024/1216), regs 1, 3 and 4

laws.rule: In England and Wales a person may not use an adult firework between 11 pm and 7 am, except on four nights: the first day of Chinese New Year, Diwali and 31 December (until 1 am the next morning) and 5 November (until midnight) (Fireworks Regulations 2004, reg 7). A person under 18 may not possess an adult firework in a public place (reg 4).
laws.heading: Fireworks Regulations 2004, regs 4 and 7 (England and Wales)

laws.rule: England's drink-driving limit is 35 micrograms of alcohol per 100 ml of breath, 80 mg per 100 ml of blood or 107 mg per 100 ml of urine (Road Traffic Act 1988, s.11(2)). Scotland's limit is lower (50 mg per 100 ml of blood).
laws.heading: Road Traffic Act 1988, s.11(2)
